mcqs.q: The proton and the electron have charges that are:
options: Equal in magnitude and opposite in sign
mcqs.why: The correct answer is equal in magnitude and opposite in sign: +1 for the proton and -1 for the electron. That is why a neutral atom, with equal numbers of each, has no net charge. The proton and neutron, meanwhile, have nearly equal masses.

lessons.title: Atomic Number, Mass Number and Isotopes
lessons.notes_html:
Structural Numbers

  • Proton number (Z) — the number of protons in the nucleus; symbol Z
  • Nucleon / Mass number (A) — the sum of protons + neutrons
  • Number of neutrons — N = A − Z

Nuclide Symbol

^A_Z X   Example: ^235_92 U

Worked Example

Find the numbers for Uranium-235.

Protons = Z = 92 ; Electrons = 92 (neutral atom)

Nucleon number = A = 235 ; Neutrons = 235 − 92 = 143

In the same way, if an element B has 5 protons and 6 neutrons, its symbol will be ^11_5 B.

Isotopes

Atoms of the same element which have the same protons but different neutrons are isotopes.

  • Examples: the three isotopes of hydrogen; the isotopes of chlorine with mass numbers 35 and 37
  • In protium the number of neutrons is zero
  • Isotopes have the same chemical properties, because their electrons and protons are the same; only physical properties such as mass are different
  • The atomic mass is approximately equal to the combined mass of the protons and neutrons

mcqs.q: The proton number (atomic number) Z is:
options: The sum of protons and neutrons
The number of electrons in an ion only
The number of protons in the nucleus
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the number of protons in the nucleus, symbol Z. It identifies the element. The mass number A is the larger quantity, the sum of protons and neutrons.

mcqs.q: The mass number (nucleon number) A is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is protons + neutrons, the total number of nucleons in the nucleus. Electrons are not counted because their mass is very small. The number of neutrons is then found as N = A - Z.

mcqs.q: The number of neutrons in an atom is found by:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is N = A - Z, subtracting the proton number from the mass number. For Uranium-235, this gives 235 - 92 = 143 neutrons. This formula is used in every nuclide problem in the notes.

mcqs.q: For Uranium-235 (^235_92 U), the numbers of protons, electrons (neutral atom) and neutrons are:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is protons 92, electrons 92, neutrons 143. Z = 92 gives both the protons and, in a neutral atom, the electrons, while the neutrons are A - Z = 235 - 92 = 143. This is the worked example in the notes.

mcqs.q: An element B has 5 protons and 6 neutrons. Its nuclide symbol is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is ^11_5 B, because A = 5 + 6 = 11 is written at the top and Z = 5 at the bottom in the symbol ^A_Z X. The notes give this exact example. Writing the numbers the wrong way round is a common error to avoid.

mcqs.q: Isotopes are atoms of the same element that have:
options: Different protons and the same neutrons
The same protons but different neutrons
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons. Examples are the three isotopes of hydrogen and the chlorine isotopes with mass numbers 35 and 37. Because their protons and electrons are the same, isotopes have the same chemical properties.

mcqs.q: Isotopes have the same chemical properties because:
options: Their electrons and protons are the same
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that their electrons and protons are the same, and chemistry depends on the electrons. Only physical properties such as mass are different between isotopes. This is stated directly in the notes on isotopes.

mcqs.q: In protium, the lightest isotope of hydrogen, the number of neutrons is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is zero: protium has only one proton and no neutron. It is the simplest of the three isotopes of hydrogen mentioned in the notes. The other isotopes differ precisely by having extra neutrons.

mcqs.q: Chlorine has isotopes with mass numbers:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 35 and 37, both with the same proton number but different neutron numbers. That difference in neutrons is what makes them isotopes of the same element. Their chemical properties remain the same.

mcqs.q: The atomic mass of an atom is approximately equal to:
options: The mass of the protons only
The combined mass of the protons and neutrons
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the combined mass of the protons and neutrons, because the electron mass is very small. This is why the mass number A = protons + neutrons gives a good measure of the atom's mass. Almost the whole mass is in the nucleus.

lessons.title: Radioactivity and Radioactive Rays
lessons.notes_html:
Radioactivity

Some heavy elements spontaneously emit rays and change into other elements. The reason is that their nucleus is unstable — in it the repulsive force of the protons exceeds the nuclear force. Elements with a stable nucleus are not radioactive. Decay is a random process: which atom will break up and when cannot be told beforehand.

Three Types of Rays

RayNatureChargeMaterial that stops it
Alpha (α)Helium nucleus (2 protons + 2 neutrons)+2A thin sheet of paper
Beta (β)Fast electron−1A few millimetres of aluminium
Gamma (γ)Electromagnetic radiation0A thick sheet of lead
  • Ionizing power — alpha the most, then beta, then gamma
  • Penetrating power — gamma the most, then beta, then alpha
  • In an electric field alpha and beta are deflected; gamma, having no charge, goes straight

mcqs.q: Radioactivity occurs because in some heavy elements the nucleus is:
options: Unstable: the repulsive force of the protons exceeds the nuclear force
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that the nucleus is unstable, with the repulsive force of the protons exceeding the nuclear force that holds it together. Such elements spontaneously emit rays and change into other elements. Elements with a stable nucleus are not radioactive.

mcqs.q: Radioactive decay is a random process. This means:
options: Decay can be stopped by cooling
Which atom will break up and when cannot be told beforehand
All atoms decay at the same fixed time
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that which atom will break up, and when, cannot be told beforehand. We can only predict how a large number of atoms behaves on average, through the half-life. Individual decays remain unpredictable.

mcqs.q: An alpha particle is:
options: A helium nucleus of 2 protons + 2 neutrons, charge +2
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a helium nucleus with 2 protons and 2 neutrons, carrying charge +2. It is the most strongly ionizing of the three rays but is stopped by a thin sheet of paper. Beta rays are fast electrons instead.

mcqs.q: Beta rays are:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is fast electrons with charge -1. They are stopped by a few millimetres of aluminium. Their ionizing power is between that of alpha and gamma rays.

mcqs.q: Gamma rays are:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is electromagnetic radiation with charge 0. Gamma rays have the greatest penetrating power and are reduced only by a thick sheet of lead. Having no charge, they are not deflected in an electric field.

mcqs.q: Alpha rays are stopped by ______; beta rays by ______; gamma rays are reduced by ______.
options: Paper only, paper only, paper only
A thin sheet of paper, a few mm of aluminium, a thick sheet of lead
mcqs.why: The correct answer is: alpha by a thin sheet of paper, beta by a few millimetres of aluminium, and gamma is reduced by a thick sheet of lead. This order matches the penetrating powers: gamma the most, then beta, then alpha. It is a standard comparison given in the notes.

mcqs.q: The ionizing power of the three rays is greatest for ______ and least for ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is alpha the most, then beta, then gamma the least. Ionizing power is the reverse order of penetrating power: alpha ionizes strongly but cannot penetrate, while gamma penetrates deeply but ionizes least. Both orders are given in the notes.

mcqs.q: In an electric field, alpha and beta rays are deflected, but gamma rays:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that gamma rays go straight because they have no charge, so the field exerts no force on them. Alpha (+2) and beta (-1) bend in opposite directions. This behaviour is a test that distinguishes the three rays.

mcqs.q: Elements with a stable nucleus are:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is not radioactive. Radioactivity appears only when the nucleus is unstable, with proton repulsion exceeding the nuclear force. Stable nuclei stay unchanged and emit no rays.

mcqs.q: The penetrating power order of the rays is:
options: Beta most, then gamma, then alpha
Gamma most, then beta, then alpha
Alpha most, then beta, then gamma
mcqs.why: The correct answer is gamma the most, then beta, then alpha. That is why a thick sheet of lead is needed to reduce gamma rays, while paper stops alpha completely. Penetrating power runs opposite to ionizing power for these rays.

lessons.title: Nuclear Equations and Half-Life
lessons.notes_html:
Decay Equations

  • Alpha decay — A decreases by 4 and Z by 2 — Radium-226 emits alpha and becomes Radon-222
  • Beta decay — A stays the same, Z increases by one (a neutron changes into a proton) — Carbon-14 emits beta and becomes Nitrogen-14
  • Gamma decay — A and Z both stay the same; only energy is emitted

The original element is called the parent and the newly formed element the daughter nuclide. Example: when Uranium-238 emits alpha, the parent is uranium and the daughter is thorium, whose proton number becomes 90 and mass number 234.

Half-Life

The time in which half the atoms of a radioactive material break up is its half-life. After every half-life the remaining quantity becomes half: from 100% to 50%, then 25%, then 12.5%, and so on.

Worked Example

The half-life of a material is 5 days. Initially it is 100 mg. How much will remain after 10 days?

10 days = 2 half-lives: 100 mg → 50 mg → 25 mg

Carbon Dating

In living things the activity of Carbon-14 stays constant; after death it starts decreasing with a half-life of 5730 years. By measuring the remaining activity the age of the sample is found. With Carbon-14, dating is possible down to about 20% remaining activity, i.e. up to about 13,000 years. For 25% of the atoms to decay (75% remaining) about 2380 years are needed.

mcqs.q: In alpha decay, the mass number A and proton number Z change as:
options: A decreases by 4 and Z decreases by 2
A increases by 4, Z increases by 2
A stays the same, Z increases by 1
mcqs.why: The correct answer is A decreases by 4 and Z decreases by 2, because an alpha particle carries away 2 protons and 2 neutrons. For example, Radium-226 emits alpha and becomes Radon-222. The new element is the daughter nuclide of the parent.

mcqs.q: In beta decay:
options: A stays the same and Z increases by one, as a neutron changes into a proton
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that A stays the same and Z increases by one, because a neutron changes into a proton and the beta particle (electron) is emitted. For example, Carbon-14 emits beta and becomes Nitrogen-14. The element changes even though the mass number does not.

mcqs.q: In gamma decay, A and Z:
options: Both stay the same; only energy is emitted
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that both stay the same and only energy is emitted. Gamma emission therefore does not change the element at all. It usually accompanies alpha or beta decay when the nucleus has extra energy.

mcqs.q: When Uranium-238 emits an alpha particle, the daughter (thorium) has:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Z = 90 and A = 234, since alpha decay reduces Z by 2 and A by 4. The original element, uranium, is called the parent and the newly formed thorium is the daughter nuclide. This is the example given in the notes.

mcqs.q: The original element in a decay is called the ______ and the newly formed element the ______.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is parent for the original element and daughter nuclide for the newly formed one. For example, when Uranium-238 emits alpha, uranium is the parent and thorium is the daughter. These names are used in writing nuclear equations.

mcqs.q: The half-life of a radioactive material is the time in which:
options: Half of its atoms break up
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the time in which half of the atoms break up. After every half-life the remaining quantity becomes half again: from 100% to 50%, then 25%, then 12.5%, and so on. The half-life is a fixed property of the material.

mcqs.q: A material has a half-life of 5 days. Starting from 100 mg, the amount remaining after 10 days is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 25 mg. Ten days is 2 half-lives, so the amount falls 100 mg -> 50 mg -> 25 mg. This is the worked example of half-life given in the notes.

mcqs.q: After three half-lives, the fraction of a radioactive sample remaining is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1/8, i.e. 12.5%, following the sequence 100% -> 50% -> 25% -> 12.5% given in the notes. Each half-life halves whatever remains. The sample never reaches exactly zero in this pattern.

mcqs.q: Carbon dating works because in living things the activity of Carbon-14 stays constant, and after death it:
options: Decreases with a half-life of 5730 years
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that it decreases with a half-life of 5730 years. By measuring the remaining activity, the age of the sample is found. With Carbon-14, dating is possible down to about 20% remaining activity, i.e. up to about 13,000 years.

mcqs.q: Carbon-14 dating is possible up to about:
options: 13,000 years, down to about 20% remaining activity
mcqs.why: The correct answer is about 13,000 years, while about 20% of the activity remains measurable. Beyond that, the remaining activity is too small to measure reliably. The notes also state that for 25% of the atoms to decay (75% remaining) about 2380 years are needed.

lessons.title: Nuclear Fission and Fusion
lessons.notes_html:
Nuclear Fission

The splitting of a heavy nucleus (e.g. Uranium-235), on being hit by a slow neutron, into two smaller nuclei is fission. In this process 3 new neutrons and a large amount of energy are released. The new neutrons break other nuclei and form a chain reaction.

  • Use — generating electricity in a nuclear power station
  • Artificial radioactive isotopes are also prepared in atomic reactors, which are used in medical and industrial work

Nuclear Fusion

The joining of two light nuclei to form one heavier nucleus is fusion. In the Sun, light nuclei join to form helium and energy is released.

  • Fusion is the source of energy of the Sun and the stars
  • Fusion needs a very high temperature (millions of degrees)
  • Per kilogram of fuel, fusion gives more energy than fission and the long-lived radioactive waste is also less, so it is a candidate for sustainable energy
FissionFusion
A heavy nucleus splitsLight nuclei join
Used in a power stationTakes place in the Sun and stars

mcqs.q: Nuclear fission is the splitting of a heavy nucleus when it is hit by:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a slow neutron. Uranium-235 splits into two smaller nuclei, releasing 3 new neutrons and a large amount of energy. Those new neutrons can split other nuclei, forming a chain reaction.

mcqs.q: In the fission of Uranium-235, the number of new neutrons released is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is three new neutrons, together with a large amount of energy. Because each fission releases more neutrons than caused it, the new neutrons break other nuclei and a chain reaction builds up. This is the process used in a nuclear power station.

mcqs.q: A chain reaction in fission is formed because:
options: Neutrons are absorbed by the walls
The new neutrons released break other nuclei, which release still more neutrons
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that the new neutrons break other nuclei, and each of those releases still more neutrons (3 per fission of U-235). The reaction therefore multiplies rapidly unless controlled. In a power station it is controlled to generate electricity steadily.

mcqs.q: Nuclear fission is used for:
options: Generating electricity in a nuclear power station
mcqs.why: The correct answer is generating electricity in a nuclear power station, where the energy of splitting heavy nuclei is converted to electrical energy. Artificial radioactive isotopes are also prepared in atomic reactors for medical and industrial work. The Sun, by contrast, works by fusion.

mcqs.q: Nuclear fusion is:
options: The splitting of a heavy nucleus
The joining of two light nuclei to form one heavier nucleus
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the joining of two light nuclei to form one heavier nucleus. In the Sun, light nuclei join to form helium and energy is released. Fusion is therefore the source of energy of the Sun and the stars.

mcqs.q: Fusion is the source of energy of:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is the Sun and the stars, where light nuclei join to form helium at enormous temperatures. Earth's nuclear power stations use fission instead. The contrast between fission and fusion is summarised in the table in the notes.

mcqs.q: Fusion requires:
options: A very high temperature of millions of degrees
mcqs.why: The correct answer is a very high temperature, of millions of degrees, so that the light nuclei can overcome their repulsion and join. Such temperatures exist naturally in the Sun and stars. Reproducing them on Earth is the main difficulty of fusion power.

mcqs.q: Per kilogram of fuel, fusion compared with fission gives:
options: The same energy and the same waste
Less energy and more long-lived waste
More energy and less long-lived radioactive waste
mcqs.why: The correct answer is more energy and less long-lived radioactive waste, so fusion is a candidate for sustainable energy. These advantages are stated in the notes. Its obstacle is the millions-of-degrees temperature it needs.

mcqs.q: Artificial radioactive isotopes are prepared in:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is atomic reactors, and the isotopes are used in medical and industrial work. Reactors exploit controlled fission to supply the neutrons needed. This is a useful by-product of fission besides electricity generation.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly pairs the process with where it happens?
options: Fission in a power station; fusion in the Sun and stars
Fission in the Sun; fusion in power stations
mcqs.why: The correct answer is fission in a power station and fusion in the Sun and stars, exactly as in the comparison table in the notes. Fission splits a heavy nucleus; fusion joins light nuclei. Keeping this pairing straight is a common examination point.

lessons.title: Hazards of Radioactive Rays and Safety
lessons.notes_html:
Harms of Radiation

  • Causing cancer
  • Genetic mutation — effect on coming generations
  • Deep burns of the skin

Radiation ionizes the cells of the body and spoils their structure. Alpha particles are stopped outside by paper and skin, but if an alpha-emitting material enters the body with food or breath it is the most dangerous, because all its energy is absorbed in the tissues inside. Gamma rays penetrate deeply and cause harm even from outside.

Safety Measures

  • Keep the material far from the body — the effect decreases rapidly as distance increases
  • Keep the time of use as short as possible
  • Use a lead screen and protective clothing
  • Hold the material with tongs and work with sealed sources
  • Wash hands thoroughly on leaving the laboratory

Management of Radioactive Waste

A large amount of radioactive waste is sealed in safe containers and buried deep inside the ground or a mountain, until its activity decreases to a safe level. Draining it away, burning it in fire or throwing it into the sea is dangerous and forbidden.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a harm of radiation given in the notes?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is causing cancer. Radiation also causes genetic mutation, affecting coming generations, and deep burns of the skin. It harms the body because it ionizes the cells and spoils their structure.

mcqs.q: Radiation harms the body because it:
options: Ionizes the cells of the body and spoils their structure
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that it ionizes the cells of the body and spoils their structure, which can lead to cancer, mutations and burns. This ionizing action is the root of all radiation damage. Safety measures all aim to reduce this exposure.

mcqs.q: Alpha-emitting material is most dangerous when it:
options: Enters the body with food or breath, because all its energy is absorbed in the tissues inside
mcqs.why: The correct answer is when it enters the body with food or breath. Outside the body, alpha particles are stopped by paper and skin, but inside, all their energy is absorbed in the tissues, doing maximum damage. This is why sealed sources and cleanliness are essential.

mcqs.q: Gamma rays are dangerous even from outside the body because they:
options: Penetrate deeply and cause harm from outside
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that they penetrate deeply and cause harm even from outside, unlike alpha particles which are stopped by the skin. This deep penetration is why distance and lead shielding are used against gamma sources. It matches gamma's greatest penetrating power.

mcqs.q: One safety measure with radioactive materials is to:
options: Keep the material far from the body, because the effect decreases rapidly with distance
Hold them in the hand for long
Use them for a long time continuously
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to keep the material far from the body, since the effect decreases rapidly as distance increases. The time of use should also be kept as short as possible. Distance and short exposure are two of the basic protections listed in the notes.

mcqs.q: Radioactive material should be held with ______ and worked with as ______ sources.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is tongs, and the sources should be sealed. A lead screen and protective clothing should also be used, and hands must be washed thoroughly on leaving the laboratory. These measures keep the material away from the body and prevent it entering by food or breath.

mcqs.q: After working with radioactive material in the laboratory, one must:
options: Wash hands thoroughly on leaving the laboratory
mcqs.why: The correct answer is to wash hands thoroughly, so no radioactive material stays on the skin or is carried to food. Protective clothing and a lead screen are used during the work itself. Such habits are part of the safety measures in the notes.

mcqs.q: Genetic mutation caused by radiation is serious because it:
options: Has an effect on coming generations
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that it has an effect on coming generations, since the damage is passed through the reproductive cells. Together with cancer and deep skin burns, it is one of the three harms listed in the notes. This long-term effect is why exposure limits are strict.

mcqs.q: Radioactive waste is managed by:
options: Sealing a large amount in safe containers and burying it deep in the ground or a mountain until its activity falls to a safe level
mcqs.why: The correct answer is sealing it in safe containers and burying it deep inside the ground or a mountain, until its activity decreases to a safe level. Draining it away, burning it in fire or throwing it into the sea is dangerous and forbidden, as stated in the notes.

mcqs.q: Keeping the time of use of a radioactive source as short as possible is a safety measure because:
options: Short use makes the source stronger
Less exposure time means less radiation dose received
mcqs.why: The correct answer is that a shorter exposure time means a smaller total dose of radiation received by the body. Combined with keeping distance and using lead shielding, it limits the ionization damage to cells. These three ideas — distance, time and shielding — run through all the safety measures in the notes.
